cast.name: Marty Kessler, Consumer Defender
cast.persona: Consumer advocate who has been on hold since the nineties. Reads fine print like scripture and fees like a list of enemies.

cast.name: Dr. Penelope Thrum
cast.persona: Professor of Phone Studies at a college nobody can find. Treats every gadget as an anthropological crisis.

cast.name: Rico Valdez, live
cast.persona: WBSY field reporter who is always live, always outside, and always slightly in the way of a bus.
catchphrases: Rico Valdez, live, back to you.

cast.persona: The station impressionist. Does every voice the same way and announces each one first, which is the only way you could tell.

lines.text: [sfx sting] WBSY Talk. It is {time} on {street}. This is The Billionaire Hour, with Buck Mercer.
Good {daypart}, Brooklyn! [beat] Today we are talking about the richest men in the world, [breath] and how they are basically just like me, [punch] minus the money.
And minus the rockets, Buck.
I have a rocket, Boards. [beat] It is a scooter. [pause 0.4] Line one, you are on the air.
Buck. Gus. [beat] Think about it. Elon Musk bought Twitter and named it X. [pause 0.5] What else is called X? [beat] The spot on the map. [em] He is hiding something under the internet.
Gus, that is insane, and I want to hear more.
He lands rockets on a boat, Buck. [beat] Backwards. [pause 0.4] Who does that? A man with a plan. Or a man who lost the instructions.
[over] It is called engineering, Gus.
That is what they want you to call it. [sfx buzz]
Gus has dropped. [beat] He does that. Line two, Tanya from the laundromat.
Buck, I want to talk about Warren Buffett. [beat] The man is one of the richest people on earth, and he lives in the same house in Omaha since the fifties.
[beat] He never moved?
Never moved, Buck. [pause 0.4] I respect that. Every landlord in this neighborhood would have turned that house into nine studios and a wellness room.
Tanya, what is his secret?
He buys good companies and then he waits. [beat] For decades. [punch] I cannot wait for the dryer.
That is the problem with this country, Boards. Nobody waits. [pause 0.4] I could be rich if I waited.
Buck, you waited forty minutes for a parking spot yesterday.
[beat] And it paid off, Boards. [em] Long term investing. Line three, Kiki.
Okay, but, like. [beat] Sam Altman. The A I guy. He got fired by his own board, and then he was back within the week.
Kiki, I have been fired from four radio stations, and none of them called back.
That is because you did not make a chatbot, Buck. [beat] If you made a chatbot, they would beg.
Boards, make a note. [pause 0.4] Buck Mercer chatbot. Never wrong, sometimes loud.
Nobody would subscribe, Buck.
I would subscribe, if it had a mute button.
[laugh] Everybody wants the mute button. [beat] One more. Kiki, crypto, yes or no?
My cousin put his whole birthday money in a coin with a frog on it. [pause 0.4] It is a dollar now. [beat] The frog is still smiling.

That frog is a businessman, Kiki. [beat] Here is what I learned today. [pause 0.5] The billionaires are not like us. They have rockets, river-cooled computers and the same house for seventy years. [punch] We have the stoop. And the stoop has never lost value.
The stoop is rented, Buck.
[beat] Back after the break.

shows.title: Phone Studies with Dr. Penelope Thrum

lines.text: [sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Block Talk Extra, with Lorraine Static.
Good {daypart}. In the studio, a woman who has studied our phones for twenty years, [beat] and would like us to stop. Doctor Penelope Thrum, Professor of Phone Studies.
Thank you, Lorraine. [beat] I want to say first, the data is upsetting.
Start with the big one. iPhone or Android.

It is not a phone, Lorraine. It is a tribe. [pause 0.5] The iPhone people speak in blue bubbles. The Android people speak in green bubbles. [beat] They have not shared a group chat peacefully since the bubbles began.
Why does the colour matter?
It should not. [beat] But in my research, a man was left out of a birthday party because his text came in green. [pause 0.5] The cake was blue.
What does Apple want, Doctor?

Apple wants you to buy a new phone every September that looks like the old phone, [breath] and a new cable for the old charger, [beat] and then a little adapter for the new cable. [punch] It is a cable ecosystem.
And Google?
Google wants to know where you are. [beat] Which is fine. Because Google always knows. [pause 0.4] Last week Google asked me to rate a restaurant I only walked past. [beat] It knew I looked at it.
Doctor, Macs or PCs.
The Mac person owns one computer and talks about it like a sports car. [beat] The PC person has opened their computer with a screwdriver, [breath] and is proud, [punch] and has one screw left over.
Which are you?
I have a Mac at work and a PC at home, [beat] and I do not trust either of them.
Young people. Gen Z. How do they use the phone?
They do not call. [pause 0.5] If the phone rings, a Gen Z person puts it face down and waits for it to stop, [beat] like a bear in the woods.
And texting?
They text a single letter. K. [beat] That letter can end a friendship. [pause 0.4] A period at the end of a sentence means you are furious.
Doctor, I put a period at the end of every sentence.
[beat] Then they think you are furious, Lorraine.
I am furious, Doctor. [beat] It is the rent.
[laugh] That is also in the data.
Any advice for our listeners?
Put the phone in a drawer for one hour a day. [pause 0.5] It will be fine. [beat] It will miss you. [punch] It will show you an ad about drawers.
Doctor Penelope Thrum, everybody. Next, the weather: {weather}.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. The Consumer Defender, with Marty Kessler.
Hello, Brooklyn. Marty Kessler. [beat] I read the fine print so you do not have to, [breath] and then I yell about it so you do not have to.
Marty, the phones are lit.
Of course they are, Boards. Everybody has been charged for something. [pause 0.4] Caller, you are on.
Marty, it is Rosa. My streaming went up again. [beat] And now it has ads. [pause 0.4] I am paying to watch ads.
Rosa, this is the oldest trick there is. [beat] They sold us streaming to get away from cable. [em] Now we have six streaming services, [breath] and together they are cable, but in more apps.
And they stopped password sharing. My sister and I have not talked since.
[beat] They broke up a family, Rosa, to save a few dollars. [pause 0.4] Cancel one a month. Rotate. Make them chase you.
Next caller, Hakim.
Marty, I flew to see my uncle. [beat] The ticket was cheap. Then the bag was money, the seat was money, [breath] the little pillow was money.
Did they charge you for the window?
They charged me for looking at the window, Marty.
[laugh] One day, Hakim, the seatbelt will be a subscription. [beat] Next!

Hi! Marty! Dev. [beat] I tried to buy concert tickets. [pause 0.4] It sold out in one minute, [breath] and then the same tickets came back for three times the price, from a man who also does not live here.
Dev, the ticket has a service fee, a facility fee, [breath] and a convenience fee. [pause 0.5] There is no convenience, Dev. [em] The fee is the convenience. For them.
Also the coffee shop screen asked me to tip on a muffin I picked up myself.
The tipping screen! [beat] Boards, cue the music.
We do not have music, Marty.
[beat] Then cue the silence. [pause 0.6] Dev, the screen turns around, [breath] the cashier looks at you, [breath] and twenty percent, twenty five, thirty are glowing at you like a slot machine.
I pressed thirty. [beat] I panicked.
Everybody panics, Dev. That is the business model. [pause 0.4] Last caller, Mrs. Delacroix.
Marty, the self-checkout at the supermarket told me there was an unexpected item in the bagging area. [beat] It was my purse.
Mrs. Delacroix, you scanned your own food, bagged your own food, [breath] and the machine accused you of a crime. [punch] You did the job for free and got a warning.
Write that down.
It is written, Mrs. Delacroix. [beat] Here is today's rule. Read every receipt. Ask for every fee to come off. [pause 0.5] And say the word manager slowly, like you are summoning something.
That is the Consumer Defender. Back after this.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Dear Lorraine, after dark. It is {time}.
Good evening, night people. [beat] The letters came in, the coffee went cold, [breath] and Boards is pretending not to listen.
I am working the board, Lorraine.
You are reading over my shoulder, Boards. [pause 0.5] First letter. Dear Lorraine. My boyfriend says he will fix the sink. [beat] He said it in March.
[beat] It is not March.
No, Boards. It is not March. [pause 0.5] Darling, when a man says he will fix it, it means the sink is now a family heirloom. [beat] Your grandchildren will inherit that drip.
Lorraine, in fairness, women say I am fine and mean the opposite.
[beat] Boards, that is true, and I am fine. [pause 0.6] Second letter. Dear Lorraine. I am a man. Every woman I date wants to know my plan for five years. [beat] I do not have a plan for Thursday.
Honey, that is your answer. [beat] Make a plan for Thursday. [punch] Then we will talk about five years.
So both sides lose.
Everybody loses, Boards. That is what makes it romance. [pause 0.5] Next. Rosa from Marcy writes, as always.
Dear Lorraine. I matched with a man on a dating app. [beat] His pictures were all from Instagram. In every one, he is holding a fish.
Rosa, the fish is a test. [beat] A man with a fish wants you to know he can wait in silence for hours. [pause 0.4] That is not a hobby. [em] That is a warning.
He took me to brunch and photographed the eggs for twenty minutes.
The eggs got the date, Rosa. [beat] You were the plus one.
Next letter. Dear Lorraine, my new roommate is vegan, and she tells me about it before I have had breakfast.
Here is the deal. [beat] The vegans can tell us about the cows, [breath] and we can tell them about the barbecue, [punch] and everybody eats at the same table and keeps it short.
That is diplomacy, Lorraine.
That is Thanksgiving, Boards. [pause 0.6] Last letter. Dear Lorraine. A young man with a mustache, a vest and a tiny hat opened a store on my block. [beat] It sells one candle.
Is it a hipster?
Baby, it is a hipster, and it is lovely. [beat] He will play you a record you never heard of, [breath] and then tell you he liked it before it was a record.
He also goes to the techno parties under the bridge.

Everybody goes to the techno parties, Boards. [beat] They wear black, they do not smile, [breath] and at six in the morning they hug the house music people, [punch] who smile too much. [pause 0.4] Balance.
That is the mail. [beat] Write in. Lorraine Static, the only show where the weather report is also a rumor.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. It is time for the Stoop Quiz, with Buck Mercer.
Good {daypart}, Brooklyn! [beat] Two contestants, two generations, [breath] one prize: [punch] a folding chair.
The chair is ours, Buck. Please bring it back.
In the red corner, Kiki, [beat] Gen Z.
Okay, but, like, hi.
In the blue corner, Gerald Pemberton, [beat] Gen X, small businessman.
Several buildings. [beat] Small business.
Question one. [pause 0.4] What is Facebook for?
Birthday messages from people I have not seen since high school, [breath] and selling a couch.
Facebook is where my aunt posts a minion with a sentence about Mondays.
[beat] Both correct! [sfx cash] Question two. Instagram. [pause 0.4] What do you post?
My food. My outfit. A photo of a sunset where I am not looking at the sunset.
The outside of my buildings. [beat] Never the inside.
[over] Never the inside, Gerald.
Question three. WhatsApp. [pause 0.4] What is in your family chat?
Forty cousins, two uncles, and a good morning picture with a rose, every single day, at five in the morning.
A voice note from my grandmother. [beat] It is eleven minutes long. [pause 0.4] The first nine minutes are her trying to find the button.
[laugh] Correct, both! Question four. [beat] Twitter.
You mean X?
Nobody calls it X.
[beat] Okay, that is the one thing Gen X and Gen Z agree on.
History, Boards! [pause 0.5] Question five, the tie breaker. [beat] Kiki, what did Gen X do for fun?
Um. [beat] Waited by a phone that was attached to a wall?
We rode bikes until it was dark and nobody knew where we were. [beat] It was wonderful. [pause 0.4] It was also very dangerous.
Gerald, what does Gen Z do for fun?
[beat] They film themselves doing a dance in a kitchen, [breath] and then do it again, [breath] and then again, [punch] because the first one had bad lighting.
That is called content, Gerald.
Bonus question! [pause 0.4] The underground warehouse party. Where is it?
It is a secret. [beat] They text you the address at midnight.
I own the warehouse.
[over] Gerald!
Gerald wins the chair, [beat] and a visit from the fire marshal. [sfx buzz] Back after the break.
[sfx sting] WBSY News. I am Dana Okafor. [beat] We go live to Rico Valdez, who is outside, as always. Rico?
Dana! Rico Valdez, live, [breath] at the turnstiles, where a man is trying to pay the fare with his face.
With his face, Rico?
The machine takes your phone, your card, your watch. [beat] He thinks it should take his face. [pause 0.4] He is leaning very close. [em] It is not working.
Rico, the fare went up again.

It did, Dana. [beat] People are upset. [pause 0.4] But a woman here told me the train is still the best deal in the city, [breath] because where else can you get a concert, a sermon and a man selling churros, for one ride.
And congestion pricing?

Driving into lower Manhattan costs money now, Dana. [beat] I asked a driver what he thinks. He said he hates it. [pause 0.4] Then he said the traffic is better. [beat] Then he said he still hates it. [punch] A true New Yorker.
Rico, watch your back.

I am watching, Dana. [beat] Delivery bikes everywhere. [pause 0.4] One just went by with four bags, a pizza on the handlebars and a man's soup in a bag around his wrist. [breath] He waved. [beat] He was also on the phone.
The apps promise thirty minutes.
The food comes in thirty minutes, Dana. [beat] The man who brings it has been on the road since sunrise, [breath] so tip him like you mean it.
Where are you headed now?
Back to the office, Dana. [beat] My company says we all have to return.
And what is at the office?
A plant. [pause 0.4] A man named Craig who microwaves fish. [beat] And a meeting about why we should be in the office, [punch] which could have been an email.
And the rent, Rico?
I walked by a one bedroom on Gates. [beat] The broker wants a fee for showing me the door. [pause 0.4] The door was a curtain.
Any landmarks today?
Tourists at the Lady Verdigris, Dana, [breath] taking pictures of the green lady, [beat] and a pigeon taking pictures of the tourists.
And the weather?
[beat] It is {weather}, Dana. I am in it. [pause 0.4] I am always in it.
Rico Valdez, live. [beat] That is the news. Lock your doors, hug your neighbours.

shows.title: Pivot Hour: Robots, Trucks and Capes

lines.text: [sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Pivot Hour. Two hosts, [beat] no agreement.
Juniper, I want to talk about the future. [beat] Self-driving cars.
Declan, let that land. [pause 0.6] And then let it go.
The Tesla is a computer with wheels. [beat] It updates overnight. [pause 0.4] It is a car that gets better while you sleep.
My car is a bicycle, Declan. [beat] It gets better when I fill the tires.
And the Cybertruck! A truck made of stainless steel! [breath] You cannot dent it.
It looks like a fridge that went to law school, Declan.
[beat] That is a feature, not a bug.
And they keep saying it will drive itself next year. [pause 0.5] They have been saying next year for a lot of years. [beat] Next year is a long time.
Okay. Open A I. You can talk to a computer, and it answers.
I talk to my plants, Declan. [beat] They do not answer, [breath] but they do not charge a monthly fee.
The chatbot wrote my wedding speech.
I was at your wedding. [pause 0.4] The speech thanked the guests for their engagement metrics.
[beat] People were engaged, Juniper.
Declan, your uncle cried. [pause 0.4] Not because it was moving. [em] Because it was eleven minutes long.
Let us pivot. [beat] Marvel movies.
Oh, hold space for me. [pause 0.5] There are so many. I have to watch nine films and two shows to understand why a man is sad about a hammer.
That is the multiverse, Juniper. Every version of the story exists.
Then somewhere there is a version where it is ninety minutes long. [beat] I want to live there.
And you have to stay for the scene after the credits.
I stayed. [pause 0.4] The scene was a man eating a sandwich, [breath] promising another movie. [beat] The cleaners asked me to leave.
Final pivot. [beat] Fashion. The sneaker resale market.
You mean the shoes from Kanye, [beat] who now goes by Ye.
Two letters. [beat] Very efficient. Very lean. I respect the rebrand.
The shoes cost as much as rent, Declan. [pause 0.4] You cannot live in a shoe. [beat] I asked.
Some people live in a shoe, Juniper. [beat] It is a nursery rhyme.
It is a warning, Declan. [pause 0.5] Let that land.
[beat] Pivot Hour. [breath] We will iterate on this after the break.
[sfx sting] WBSY News. The World, Briefly. I am Dana Okafor, [beat] and I will be brief, because the world is not.
Abroad. [pause 0.4] Vladimir Putin appeared again at the far end of a very long table. [beat] Our studio table is two feet long. [punch] We sit very close. We do not like it.
In fairness, Dana, he also has the horse photos.
[beat] Yes, Boards. The famous photographs on a horse, with no shirt. [pause 0.4] Our weatherman has asked to do the forecast that way. [em] Request denied.
In television. [beat] A rerun of a Charlie Sheen sitcom is playing right now, on some channel, somewhere. [pause 0.4] Scientists cannot find a moment in the last twenty years when one was not.
The reruns are a natural resource, Dana.
They are, Boards. [beat] Like wind, or tides, or the man on Throop who is always washing his car.
In politics. [pause 0.4] The president signed something with a very large marker. [beat] Our producer has the same marker. [punch] He uses it to label his lunch.
Nobody touches the lunch, Dana.

City Hall. [beat] The mayor still wants free buses. [pause 0.4] A caller from Macon blames this for the price of eggs. [breath] A caller from Lewis credits it for her new knee. [beat] Neither is how buses work.
Markets. [pause 0.4] Stocks went up after a company said A I on a phone call, [breath] and down after another company said it with less confidence.
Weather. [beat] It is {weather}, [breath] and our weather desk is taking it personally.
Transit. [beat] The G train arrived on time this morning. [pause 0.5] Officials are looking into it.
Dana, there was a rumor it was a different train painted green.
[beat] We cannot confirm that, Boards. [pause 0.4] We can confirm it was green.
Culture. [beat] A new superhero movie opened this weekend. [pause 0.4] It is the second part of the third part of the first part. [beat] Reviewers recommend bringing notes.
That is the world, briefly. [beat] Lock your doors, hug your neighbours.
Now, a WBSY bit. Our station impressionist, Vinnie Impressions, does his impression of Warren Buffett. [beat] Not the real one, obviously. Vinnie has never been to Nebraska.
Here is my impression. [pause 0.4] Ahem.
Well now. [beat] Pull up a stoop. [breath] Here in Bed-Stuy, I like to buy a good bodega and hold it forever.
Vinnie, you cannot buy a bodega forever.
You can if you never stop buying the chopped cheese, Lorraine. [beat] That is called a moat. [pause 0.4] The moat is the line out the door.
What about crypto, Mister Impression?
Well, a coin with a frog on it is not a business. [beat] A frog is not a business. [punch] A frog is a frog.
And the rent?
I have lived in the same apartment for many, many years. [pause 0.4] The secret is to never call the landlord. [beat] If he does not hear from you, he forgets the lease exists.
That is not investing advice, Vinnie.
No, Lorraine. [beat] It is stoop advice. Stoop advice has a much better return.
Mister Impression, what about the A I stocks everybody is buying?
Well, Lorraine, I like to buy things I understand. [beat] I understand a dollar slice. [pause 0.4] I do not understand a computer that writes poems about it.
And the market? Up or down?
The market goes up, and the market goes down, [breath] and the stoop stays exactly where it is. [beat] Be the stoop, Lorraine.
Be the stoop. [pause 0.4] Vinnie, that is the most profound thing you have ever said, and you said it in a borrowed voice.
One more thing. [beat] Never buy a sandwich from a man who tells you it is an investment.
Who told you that?
[beat] Nobody, Lorraine. I made it up. That is the impression. And that was my impression.
That was Vinnie Impressions doing his impression of Warren Buffett. [pause 0.4] Not the real one, obviously. The real one has a better accent and a lot more bodegas.
Introducing Premium Moon. [beat] Get the blue check on your night sky.
Verified tides. Priority eclipses. [pause 0.4] Fewer ads in the craters.
Premium Moon. [beat] Not affiliated with any rocket man. [punch] The moon did not agree to this.
Open Door Locksmiths. [beat] We are called Open, [breath] and we never open anything.
Our robot locksmith will explain, in a calm voice, why your door is closed. [pause 0.4] For a monthly fee.
Open Door. [beat] Unrelated to Open A I, [punch] which we also cannot open.
Is your family divided by charger cables? [pause 0.4] Reunite them, with the Cable Family Reunion Kit.
Forty seven adapters, [breath] one for every phone your uncle has ever owned. [beat] Including the one that folded.
Cable Family. [beat] Nobody leaves the cookout at four percent.
Want to be rich like the old man in Omaha? [beat] Learn patience, with Mister Oak.
Mister Oak is a tree. [pause 0.4] He has been sitting in the same spot for eighty years. [breath] He has never once checked the market.
Mister Oak. Not affiliated with Warren Buffett, [beat] or with anybody. He is a tree.
Phase Forty Recliners. [beat] Built for superhero movies that never end.
Heated seat. Snack drawer. [pause 0.4] A little button that tells you which movie this is.
Phase Forty. [beat] Marvel did not make this chair. [punch] It is only here for the scene after the credits.
Back to the office? [beat] Try Nerve Pass.
A recording of your living room, played at your desk, [breath] so you feel home while your boss feels heard.
Nerve Pass. [beat] Includes the sound of your own couch.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Bed-Stuy Talk Radio. Where the neighborhood talks back.
Buck Mercer here. Stay with us. The next segment is already arguing.
[sfx sting] You are listening to WBSY Talk. It is {time} on {street}.
Do not touch that dial. Boards just cleaned it.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Invented hosts, invented callers, very real rent.
Buck here. If you just tuned in, you missed nothing. You will miss it again later.
[sfx sting] This is WBSY Talk, Bed-Stuy. If you can hear us, the stoop has signal.
More WBSY in a moment. Hydrate. Call your landlord. No, do not.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. Opinions delivered fresh, like a bodega sandwich.
Buck Mercer. Back after this, because I am right.
[sfx sting] WBSY. Bed-Stuy Talk. Never wrong, sometimes loud.
Stay tuned. Boards says we have content. I say we have opinions.
[sfx sting] You are tuned to WBSY Talk. The phones are open. Please do not call.
That was a show. Here comes another. Nobody here plans ahead.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk. The only station where the weather report is also a rumor.
Buck here. {weather} out there. Stay inside with us.
[sfx sting] WBSY Talk, {daypart} edition. Stay right there.
Still WBSY. Still talking. Still not sorry.
[sfx sting] WBSY. Talk radio for people who talk back to the radio.
Buck Mercer. The break is short. My patience is shorter.
